note: Dual CYP17A1/AR inhibitors (galeterone, seviteronel, ODM-204) were built on prostate-cancer xenografts carrying AR-degradation or lyase-selectivity claims; galeterone's AR-V7 degradation went into a biomarker-selected phase 3 that stopped for futility, seviteronel failed after enzalutamide, ODM-204 was PK-limited; abiraterone and enzalutamide are context only, not members.
label: Prostate cancer (CYP17A1/AR dual inhibitors)

engagement.model: LAPC4 androgen-dependent xenografts in SCID mice (galeterone, then VN/124-1)
engagement.note: VN/124-1 inhibited CYP17 (IC50 300 nM), antagonised wild-type and mutant AR, and cut LAPC4 tumour volume 93.8%; no patient comparison yet.
engagement.short: CYP17/AR dual hit shrinks LAPC4 xenografts
engagement.quote: Compound 5 (50 mg/kg/twice daily) resulted in a 93.8% reduction (P = 0.00065) in the mean final tumor volume compared with controls, and it was also significantly more effective than castration.

engagement.model: CWR22Rv1 cells and castration-resistant xenografts (full-length and AR-V7 degradation)
engagement.note: Galeterone degraded full-length and truncated AR in CWR22Rv1 cells (xenografts in 2015); AR-V7 protein loss was never measured in treated patients.
engagement.short: AR-V7 degradation never read in patients
engagement.quote: Importantly, we also discovered that our compounds, including 5, 36, 43, and 47, could degrade both full-length and truncated ARs in CWR22rv1 human prostate cancer cells.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of the model papers; the ARMOR2 AR-V7 cohort exists only as ASCO abstracts and was not used.
engagement.judgement: Kwegyir-Afful 2015 (doi 10.18632/oncotarget.4578) carried the AR/AR-V7 degradation into CRPC xenografts. ARMOR3-SV (Taplin 2019, doi 10.1016/j.eururo.2019.08.034) selected patients on CTC AR-V7 mRNA but its abstract reports no on-treatment AR-V7 change, so the model's own PD read-out was never compared in patients; the PSA fall in unselected CRPC is scored on the LAPC4 track.

engagement.model: Enzalutamide-resistant LNCaP-derived (MR49F) and MDA-PCa-133 patient-derived xenografts in castrate mice
engagement.note: VT-464 cut intratumoral androgens and AR output in enzalutamide-resistant MR49F xenografts more than abiraterone; patient PD not yet compared.
engagement.quote: In vivo, intratumoral androgen levels were significantly lower after VT-464 or AA treatment compared with vehicle, with the greatest decrease seen with VT-464.

engagement.model: LAPC4 androgen-dependent xenografts in SCID mice (galeterone, then VN/124-1)
engagement.note: PSA fell at least 50% in 11/49 (ARMOR1) and 12/25 (ARMOR2 part 1); authors call the PD changes consistent with AR-signalling inhibition.  Retrodiction rule: CYP17A1 inhibition lowering androgens in patients was public from abiraterone (O'Donnell 2004, doi 10.1038/sj.bjc.6601879) before this model, so a reproduction scores retro.
engagement.short: PSA fell 50% or more in 22-48% of patients
engagement.quote: Galeterone was well tolerated and demonstrated pharmacodynamic changes consistent with its selective, multifunctional AR signaling inhibition.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the hormone and AR-protein PD data behind the authors' sentence are not itemised in the abstract, so PSA (downstream) is the read-out scored.
engagement.reason: PSA fell; PD matched AR inhibition
engagement.judgement: The model's PD read-out was AR protein down-regulation and CYP17 inhibition in LAPC4 tumours (Vasaitis 2008); the patient read-out available at abstract level is PSA, the AR-output gene, so readout_tier is downstream and the comparison is paired, not stated. ARMOR1 (NCT00959959) and ARMOR2 (NCT01709734) never posted registry results.
engagement.magnitude_basis: PSA decline as the AR-output read-out

engagement.model: Enzalutamide-resistant LNCaP-derived (MR49F) and MDA-PCa-133 patient-derived xenografts in castrate mice
engagement.note: One mCRPC patient on VT-464 showed DHEA and PSA falls reported beside the MDA-PCa-133 PDX result; the lyase-product read-out moved in a human.  Retrodiction rule: CYP17A1 inhibition lowering androgens in patients was public from abiraterone (O'Donnell 2004, doi 10.1038/sj.bjc.6601879) before this model, so a reproduction scores retro.
engagement.short: DHEA and PSA fell in one patient
engagement.quote: Administration of VT-464 in a metastatic CRPC patient presenting with high tumoral expression of both androgen receptor (AR) and CYP17A1, showed significant reduction in the level of both dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) and serum PSA.
engagement.confidence_note: n = 1 patient, reported inside the model paper; abstract-level reading.
engagement.reason: DHEA fell in a dosed patient
engagement.judgement: The phase 1 in CRPC (Gupta 2018, doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-18-0564) listed endocrine results as a secondary objective but its abstract gives no numbers, so the single-patient Maity report is the quoted comparison. Yin 2017 (doi 10.1124/dmd.117.075317) found no lyase selectivity in side-by-side enzymology; that bears on the mineralocorticoid claim in safety, not on engagement.

engagement.model: Cynomolgus monkey and hCG-treated rat adrenal/testicular steroidogenesis, with rodent and primate tolerability
engagement.note: Monkeys and rats showed dose-dependent adrenal and testicular steroid suppression after ODM-204; castrate mCRPC patients showed further testosterone falls. Re-keyed from the VCaP xenograft track: the read-out is the monkey and rat steroidogenesis system.  Retrodiction rule: CYP17A1 inhibition lowering androgens in patients was public from abiraterone (O'Donnell 2004, doi 10.1038/sj.bjc.6601879) before this model, so a reproduction scores retro.
engagement.quote: Decreases in testosterone levels were seen with ODM-204 treatment confirming androgen deprivation.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the size of the testosterone fall is not in the abstract. Model first public 2018 (Oksala epub 2018-02-10); NCT02344017 started 2015-02, so first use was earlier but undated.
engagement.judgement: No untested opener: the model paper (Oksala, epub Feb 2018) and the trial paper (epub Sep 2018) share the year. Testosterone is the product of the CYP17 pathway, so the read-out is proximal; the comparison is mine, the trial paper does not cite the monkey data.

engagement.model: Recombinant CYP17A1 17alpha-hydroxylase-vs-17,20-lyase enzyme assay rating VT-464 lyase-selective (in-vitro biochemical system)
engagement.note: Enzyme assays rated VT-464 lyase-selective, predicting androgen suppression with cortisol spared; no patient steroid profile yet.
engagement.short: Lyase-selective inhibitor spares cortisol in vitro
engagement.quote: Herein, we describe rationally-designed, CYP17 lyase-selective inhibitors that could prove safer and more effective than abiraterone.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the paper is the medicinal-chemistry disclosure of VT-464 (compound 6). model_kind is ex_vivo because the enum has no in-vitro value; the system is a biochemical enzyme assay, not patient cells.
engagement.judgement: Opener. The system is the hydroxylase-vs-lyase biochemical assay, a different model with a different prediction (cortisol sparing, no steroid replacement) from the growth xenografts the draft tracks, which fold the claim into an inferred note.

engagement.model: Recombinant CYP17A1 17alpha-hydroxylase-vs-17,20-lyase enzyme assay rating VT-464 lyase-selective (in-vitro biochemical system)
engagement.note: One mCRPC patient on VT-464 300 mg twice daily without prednisone: adrenal androgens fell, cortisol unchanged over 40 months, the selectivity the assay predicted.
engagement.quote: Analysis of blood plasma of VT-464 treated patient demonstrated VT-464 effectively inhibited adrenal androgen production but not cortisol during entire 40 months of treatment.
engagement.confidence_note: n = 1; open-access full text read. The trial is not named; Innocrin's VT-464 phase 1/2 twice-daily study (NCT02012920, completed) posted no results. Yin 2017 (doi 10.1124/dmd.117.075317) found no lyase selectivity in side-by-side enzyme assays, so the model claim itself was disputed in vitro.
engagement.judgement: A different prediction from the draft's Maity entry on the xenograft track (androgen and PSA fall): here the read-out is the hydroxylase product cortisol staying put while lyase products fell, the assay's selectivity claim. Proximal because both are CYP17A1 products. Model and patient data sit in one paper, so comparison_stated true.
engagement.magnitude_basis: plasma adrenal androgens vs cortisol under treatment, one patient
engagement.population: mCRPC with bone metastases, VT-464 without prednisone

dose.model: LAPC4 androgen-dependent xenografts in SCID mice (galeterone, then VN/124-1)
dose.note: Mouse regimen 50 mg/kg twice daily, half-life 44 min; the human 2,550 mg/d dose was set on PSA and PK, not on model exposure.
dose.short: No exposure target carried to patients
dose.quote: both compounds were cleared rapidly from plasma (terminal half-lives of 44.17 and 39.93 min, respectively), and neither was detectable at 8 h.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; mouse plasma levels were sub-ng/mL at a dose that still regressed tumours, and no paper converts them into a human exposure target.
dose.judgement: Montgomery 2016 (doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-15-1432) chose the 2,550 mg/d tablet dose from PSA response, safety and PK across ARMOR1 and ARMOR2 part 1; no source compares that exposure with the mouse-effective exposure, so the class-level track stays untested rather than being scored on a dose the model never set.

dose.model: CWR22Rv1 cells and castration-resistant xenografts (full-length and AR-V7 degradation)
dose.note: Cell and xenograft work set no exposure target; the phase 3 later ran at the clinically chosen 2,550 mg/d.
dose.quote: Importantly, we also discovered that our compounds, including 5, 36, 43, and 47, could degrade both full-length and truncated ARs in CWR22rv1 human prostate cancer cells.

dose.model: Enzalutamide-resistant LNCaP-derived (MR49F) and MDA-PCa-133 patient-derived xenografts in castrate mice
dose.note: Oral VT-464 in MR49F mice with no human exposure target stated; phase 1 later set 600 mg once daily as the RP2D by tolerability.
dose.short: RP2D set by tolerability, not the model
dose.quote: The MR49F xenograft model was used to compare effects of oral VT-464 treatment to vehicle and abiraterone acetate (AA).

dose.note: Exposure rose only up to 300 mg twice daily and fell on repeat dosing from 200 mg; PK, not toxicity, stopped ODM-204.
dose.quote: The pharmacokinetic properties of the molecule, however, prevent further development.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the monkey-effective exposure is not quoted, so the shortfall is inferred from the sponsor's PK verdict and the AUC plateau at 300 mg with loss on day 8. Model first public 2018 (Oksala epub 2018-02-10); NCT02344017 started 2015-02, so first use was earlier but undated.
dose.judgement: Table row 'target never reached in humans (PK)': dose contra, efficacy untested. The 13% PSA50 (3 of 23, with prednisone) is recorded in the efficacy note and not scored. NCT02344017 (DUALIDES) posted no results.

dose.model: ODM-204 oral-absorption models: in-vitro dissolution, TIM-1 dynamic gut model and PBPK simulation (dose linearity 50-500 mg, food effect at 200 mg, particle size)
dose.note: Dissolution, TIM-1 and PBPK models of ODM-204 absorption built to predict dose linearity, food effect and particle-size gains before the comparison.
dose.quote: The validity of the predictive methods was evaluated against the in vivo clinical pharmacokinetic (PK) data obtained after administration of the first test formulation, T1.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract and ScienceDirect preview only (paywalled). model_first_use_year is the publication year; the modelling was done during development before the 2018 PK verdict. Subjects are patients because the 50-500 mg range is the DUALIDES CRPC phase 1 (NCT02344017, no results posted) and the paper says 'in patients'.
dose.judgement: Opener on an in-silico track; the same paper carries the comparison, so the opener and the scored entry share the year, as the merge convention allows.
dose.population: mCRPC, phase 1 DUALIDES (NCT02344017), ODM-204 50-500 mg twice daily with prednisone

dose.model: ODM-204 oral-absorption models: in-vitro dissolution, TIM-1 dynamic gut model and PBPK simulation (dose linearity 50-500 mg, food effect at 200 mg, particle size)
dose.note: Run against the phase 1 PK already in hand: the three tools reproduced dose-dependent absorption and the 200 mg food effect; formulation T2 never dosed.
dose.quote: Our study shows that the predictive tools of in vitro dissolution, TIM-1 system and the PBPK (physiologically based pharmacokinetic) simulation, showed predictive power of different mechanisms of bioavailability and together provided valuable information for decision making.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; no fold-error numbers visible, so magnitude null. A 2023 food-effect review (doi 10.1016/j.ijpharm.2023.122758, ScienceDirect preview) cites it as showing TIM-1 was 'a more reliable predictor of fasted/fed pharmacokinetics' than compendial set-ups.
dose.judgement: Retrodiction: the clinical PK of formulation T1 (Peltola 2020: AUC rose only to 300 mg and fell on day 8) was known before the models were evaluated, so retro, not same. Each tool captured a different mechanism, hence partial. The prospective prediction for milled formulation T2 was never tested because PK stopped the drug, so no fresh prospective entry. This track sets no exposure target; the PK failure itself stays scored on the VCaP track.
dose.reason: Reproduced known PK; prospective prediction untested
dose.population: mCRPC, phase 1 DUALIDES (NCT02344017), ODM-204 50-500 mg twice daily with prednisone

efficacy.model: LAPC4 androgen-dependent xenografts in SCID mice (galeterone, then VN/124-1)
efficacy.note: Androgen-dependent LAPC4 xenografts regressed on VN/124-1 more than on castration; a model of hormone-sensitive, not castration-resistant, growth.
efficacy.quote: When tested in vivo, 5 proved to be very effective at inhibiting the growth of androgen-dependent LAPC4 human prostate tumor xenograft, while 6 was ineffective.

efficacy.model: CWR22Rv1 cells and castration-resistant xenografts (full-length and AR-V7 degradation)
efficacy.note: Galeterone degraded full-length and truncated AR in CWR22Rv1 cells, the basis for predicting activity in AR-V7-positive disease.
efficacy.quote: Importantly, we also discovered that our compounds, including 5, 36, 43, and 47, could degrade both full-length and truncated ARs in CWR22rv1 human prostate cancer cells.

efficacy.model: Enzalutamide-resistant LNCaP-derived (MR49F) and MDA-PCa-133 patient-derived xenografts in castrate mice
efficacy.note: Enzalutamide-resistant MR49F xenografts shrank more on VT-464 than on abiraterone, the prediction later taken into post-enzalutamide patients.
efficacy.quote: Similarly, tumor growth inhibition and PSA decrease trends were greater with VT-464 than with AA.

efficacy.model: LAPC4 androgen-dependent xenografts in SCID mice (galeterone, then VN/124-1)
efficacy.note: Treatment-naive CRPC: PSA50 22% in ARMOR1 and 48% in ARMOR2 part 1, 55% at 2,550 mg; the class-level activity the xenografts foresaw. Retrodiction rule: CYP17 inhibition with AR blockade lowering PSA in castration-resistant patients was public from ketoconazole and abiraterone (O'Donnell 2004) before the 2005 LAPC4 paper, so retro.
efficacy.quote: In ARMOR2 part 1, across all doses, PSA30 was 64.0% (16/25) and PSA50 was 48.0% (12/25).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; single-arm PSA response in 25-49 patients, no radiographic endpoint.
efficacy.reason: Naive CRPC responded as xenografts implied
efficacy.judgement: Scored on ARMOR2 part 1, whose registered primary outcome was PSA response (NCT01709734); ARMOR1's primary was safety. The LAPC4 xenografts were androgen-dependent, so this is class-level evidence that the CYP17/AR dual hit works on AR-driven tumours, not a CRPC model prediction; Vasaitis 2008 (doi 10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-08-0230) showed VN/124-1 regressing established LAPC4 tumours and down-regulating AR protein. The 2019 AR-V7 failure sits on its own track and does not turn this one.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: tumour regression in mice vs PSA50 rate in patients

patient_trials.quote: In ARMOR1, across all doses, 49.0% (24/49) achieved a ≥30% decline in prostate-specific antigen (PSA; PSA30) and 22.4% (11/49) demonstrated a ≥50% PSA decline (PSA50).
In the 2,550-mg dose cohort, PSA30 was 72.7% (8/11) and PSA50 was 54.5% (6/11).

efficacy.note: VCaP xenografts shrank on ODM-204; the phase 1/2 saw 13% PSA50 but exposure never reached target, so efficacy is not scored.
efficacy.quote: In our study, ODM-204 inhibited the proliferation of androgen-dependent VCaP and LNCaP cells in vitro and reduced significantly tumour growth in a murine VCaP xenograft model in vivo.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both the model and the trial paper. Model first public 2018 (Oksala epub 2018-02-10); NCT02344017 started 2015-02, so first use was earlier but undated.
efficacy.judgement: By the dose table a PK failure withholds the efficacy verdict; the 13% PSA50 at week 12 (Peltola 2020, doi 10.1016/j.euf.2018.08.022) came in 23 patients dosed with prednisone and is recorded here only as a note.

efficacy.model: CWR22Rv1 cells and castration-resistant xenografts (full-length and AR-V7 degradation)
efficacy.note: AR-V7+ mCRPC: trial stopped for futility; PSA50 2/16 (13%) on galeterone vs 8/19 (42%) on enzalutamide, against the degradation prediction. Dated 2016: Tokai's 2016-07-26 release announced the monitoring committee's futility call; Taplin 2019 is the tier-1 record that sets the status.
efficacy.quote: Owing to high censorship for the rPFS events, the data monitoring committee recommended early closure based on interim evidence that the primary endpoint would not be met.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; only 38 of 148 planned were randomised and rPFS was never formally tested, so the miss rests on the DMC futility call plus the PSA50 secondary.
efficacy.reason: AR-V7+ patients did worse than on enzalutamide
efficacy.judgement: The classic patient-level miss: AR/AR-V7 degradation in CWR22Rv1 cells and xenografts (Purushottamachar 2013; Kwegyir-Afful 2015) became the stated hypothesis that galeterone would beat enzalutamide in AR-V7+ mCRPC, and the paper carries both, so comparison_stated is true. Futility was first public in Tokai's press release of 2016-07-26 (tier 5); the 2019 paper sets the status and the year because press releases are not in the dating list. Alyamani 2017 (doi 10.1016/j.chembiol.2017.05.020) later showed 3βHSD/SRD5A metabolism strips galeterone of several activities, a candidate explanation. Magnitude is direction_only, not opposite: the PSA50 difference's CI crosses zero.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: PSA50 13% vs 42% (secondary); rPFS futility at interim

patient_trials.quote: The PSA50 values were 2/16 (13%) and 8/19 (42%) for galeterone and enzalutamide respectively (proportion difference=-0.278, 95% CI -0.490 to 0.097).

efficacy.model: Enzalutamide-resistant LNCaP-derived (MR49F) and MDA-PCa-133 patient-derived xenografts in castrate mice
efficacy.note: Post-enzalutamide mCRPC: 1/17 (6%) PSA50 at the primary 12-week read and closure for toxicity; the enzalutamide-resistant xenograft prediction failed. Retrodiction: abiraterone after enzalutamide had already shown little activity (2013), so the model ran after a patient result and failed to reproduce it; contra stands.
efficacy.quote: Seviteronel was not generally well tolerated nor associated with significant clinical responses in patients with mCRPC who had previously received enzalutamide.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; toxicity-driven discontinuation after a median of 2 cycles confounds the 12-week PSA50 read-out, but the source itself judges the responses absent and single-agent development unwarranted.
efficacy.judgement: Norris 2017 (doi 10.1172/JCI87328) made the same prediction with AR-F876L xenografts, an enzalutamide-resistance mutation, and is folded in here rather than given a track because it is the same prediction from a sibling model. The registry record matching this trial is not named in the abstract; NCT02445976 (post-enzalutamide/abiraterone, PCCTC) is the likely one and neither it nor NCT02012920 posted results, so registry_date is null.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: PSA50 1/17 vs xenograft tumour growth inhibition

patient_trials.quote: One (6%) of 17 patients experienced a significant decline in prostate-specific antigen.

efficacy.model: Circulating-tumour-cell AR-variant assays in patients (Epic Sciences AR C-terminal-loss protein in ARMOR2; Johns Hopkins AdnaTest AR-V7 mRNA in ARMOR3-SV) used to choose galeterone recipients
efficacy.note: Tokai's retrospective ARMOR2 analysis: 6/7 CRPC patients with CTC AR C-terminal loss had PSA50 responses; the prospective AR-V7-selected test had not run. Dated 2014: the CTC AR-variant subset (6/7 PSA responders) was first presented at EORTC-NCI-AACR, 19 Nov 2014, alongside the ARMOR2 PSA results, so not a retrodiction.
efficacy.quote: Tokai conducted a retrospective study of their phase 2 clinical data and reported positive clinical data in patients with AR C-terminal loss, showing PSA50 response in 6 of 7 (85.7% response) CRPC patients with AR C-terminal loss
efficacy.confidence_note: Second-hand record: the subset analysis was presented at EORTC-NCI-AACR 2014 (conference, no admissible tier) and is reported in this tier-1 paper citing Tokai; the ARMOR2 paper (Montgomery 2016) could not be opened to confirm it.
efficacy.judgement: Opener for a patient-level system: patient-derived circulating tumour cells assayed for AR C-terminal loss to pick galeterone recipients. The 6/7 figure is hypothesis-generating patient data, not a model prediction, so untested; the prediction it set (AR-variant-positive patients respond to galeterone) went into ARMOR3-SV. First admissible record is 2015; the draft's ODM-204 convention of dating first use at publication is followed.
efficacy.population: CRPC with CTC AR C-terminal loss (AR-V7) in ARMOR2 (NCT01709734, no results posted)

efficacy.model: Circulating-tumour-cell AR-variant assays in patients (Epic Sciences AR C-terminal-loss protein in ARMOR2; Johns Hopkins AdnaTest AR-V7 mRNA in ARMOR3-SV) used to choose galeterone recipients
efficacy.note: ARMOR3-SV: 953 prescreened by CTC AR-V7 mRNA, 38 randomised; DMC closed for futility, PSA50 2/16 galeterone vs 8/19 enzalutamide. Dated 2016: Tokai's 2016-07-26 release announced the monitoring committee's futility call; Taplin 2019 is the tier-1 record that sets the status.
efficacy.quote: Owing to high censorship for the rPFS events, the data monitoring committee recommended early closure based on interim evidence that the primary endpoint would not be met.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed). Futility was first public in Tokai's 2016-07-26 release (tier 5, SEC filing); this tier-1 paper sets the status and the draft's dating convention is followed (adjudicator rule question 2). The assay changed between hypothesis (Epic protein C-terminal loss) and test (AdnaTest AR-V7 mRNA).
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level miss on its own system: patient-derived CTC AR-variant assays chose the population, and the selected population did worse on galeterone than on enzalutamide. Paired, not stated: Taplin 2019 attributes the hypothesis to AR degradation, not to the ARMOR2 subset, so model_src is Kwegyir-Afful 2015. A separate track from the CWR22Rv1 cell/xenograft system that made the same prediction from a different model; both are scored on the same trial.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: PSA50 13% galeterone vs 42% enzalutamide in AR-V7+ mCRPC against predicted superiority
efficacy.population: AR-V7+ (CTC mRNA) enzalutamide-, abiraterone- and chemotherapy-naive mCRPC

patient_trials.quote: The PSA50 values were 2/16 (13%) and 8/19 (42%) for galeterone and enzalutamide respectively (proportion difference=-0.278, 95% CI -0.490 to 0.097).

safety.model: CWR22Rv1 cells and castration-resistant xenografts (full-length and AR-V7 degradation)
safety.note: Cell work carries no tolerability statement; the xenograft follow-up (2015) reported no apparent host toxicity at effective doses.
safety.quote: Importantly, we also discovered that our compounds, including 5, 36, 43, and 47, could degrade both full-length and truncated ARs in CWR22rv1 human prostate cancer cells.

safety.model: Enzalutamide-resistant LNCaP-derived (MR49F) and MDA-PCa-133 patient-derived xenografts in castrate mice
safety.note: Xenograft papers report no tolerability data; the stated safety claim was lyase selectivity sparing cortisol, hence no prednisone.
safety.short: Model silent on CNS; promised no mineralocorticoid excess
safety.quote: These preclinical results suggest greater suppression of the AR axis with VT-464 than ABI that is likely due to both superior selective suppression of androgen synthesis and AR antagonism.

safety.model: CWR22Rv1 cells and castration-resistant xenografts (full-length and AR-V7 degradation)
safety.note: Xenograft mice showed 'no apparent host toxicities'; patients were well tolerated without steroids and had no mineralocorticoid excess, but liver-enzyme rises went unflagged.
safety.short: Tolerated as mice implied; liver enzymes unflagged
safety.quote: Galeterone was well tolerated; the most common adverse events were fatigue, increased liver enzymes, gastrointestinal events, and pruritus.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the mouse statement is a bare 'no apparent host toxicities' with no liver chemistry, and the patient liver-enzyme rises were mostly mild.
safety.reason: Tolerated, no mineralocorticoid excess; ALT unflagged
safety.judgement: Same, not contra: the model's stated prediction (no host toxicity at effective doses, Kwegyir-Afful 2015) matched clinical tolerability, including steroid-free dosing with no apparent mineralocorticoid excess, and the ARMOR3-SV DMC cited no safety concern (Tokai 2016-07-26). Scored partial because mouse silence on liver enzymes was contradicted by a harm mice could show, though it was mostly mild and required no action.
safety.magnitude_basis: tolerability at effective dose; mineralocorticoid excess absent

safety.model: Enzalutamide-resistant LNCaP-derived (MR49F) and MDA-PCa-133 patient-derived xenografts in castrate mice
safety.note: Imported-harm ruling: prostate patients were measured in 2018 (no DLT through 750 mg, mostly grade 1-2 fatigue, dizziness, blurred vision), so the breast-cancer delirium DLTs (Bardia 2018) no longer set this entry; the silent model is not contradicted yet.
safety.quote: Once-daily seviteronel was generally well tolerated in this phase I study of men with CRPC, a majority of which had progressed on prior AA or enzalutamide, or both.
safety.confidence_note: Imported from breast cancer; the prostate phase 1 (Gupta 2018, doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-18-0564) the same year reported dizziness 52% and blurred vision 38% without DLTs through 750 mg.
safety.magnitude_basis: CNS dose-limiting toxicity vs model silence
safety.population: Chemotherapy-naive CRPC, most after abiraterone or enzalutamide

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey and hCG-treated rat adrenal/testicular steroidogenesis, with rodent and primate tolerability
safety.note: Rodents and primates tolerated ODM-204; patients had mild fatigue, appetite change and nausea up to 500 mg twice daily, with prednisone on board. Re-keyed from the VCaP xenograft track: the read-out is the monkey and rat steroidogenesis system.
safety.quote: ODM-204 was well tolerated up to the highest evaluated dose.
safety.confidence_note: Prednisone was co-administered throughout, so mineralocorticoid excess was not testable; abstract-level reading. Model first public 2018 (Oksala epub 2018-02-10); NCT02344017 started 2015-02, so first use was earlier but undated.
safety.judgement: Oksala 2019 states 'ODM-204 was well tolerated in both rodents and primates'; 23 patients up to 500 mg twice daily matched it. Same-year model and trial papers, so no untested opener.

safety.model: Enzalutamide-resistant LNCaP-derived (MR49F) and MDA-PCa-133 patient-derived xenografts in castrate mice
safety.note: In mCRPC itself, concentration impairment, tremor and fatigue drove discontinuation after a median of 2 cycles and closed the phase 2.
safety.short: CNS toxicity closed the prostate phase 2
safety.quote: Despite changes in dosing, the study was closed prematurely because of the high magnitude of toxicity.
safety.reason: CNS toxicity the mice never showed
safety.judgement: The stated prediction (lyase selectivity, no mineralocorticoid excess, steroid-free dosing) held as far as the abstracts show, so the contra rests on the unstated CNS harm; a mouse could have shown tremor or ataxia. Counted once here, not in dose, because the model set no tolerability margin (decision 16).
safety.magnitude_basis: trial closure for CNS toxicity vs model silence

safety.model: Recombinant CYP17A1 17alpha-hydroxylase-vs-17,20-lyase enzyme assay rating VT-464 lyase-selective (in-vitro biochemical system)
safety.note: Prediction: lyase selectivity avoids glucocorticoid depletion, so no prednisone and no mineralocorticoid excess; untested in patients.
safety.quote: As a consequence of potent CYP17 hydroxylase inhibition (i.e., lack of lyase selectivity), AA must be co-administered with the cortisol replacement prednisone and patients may experience the effects of mineralocorticoid excess syndrome (MES).
safety.judgement: Opener; the harm the assay speaks to is adrenal (cortisol loss, mineralocorticoid excess). A biochemical assay has no species, so later CNS harms are not its silence to score; they stay on the xenograft track.

safety.model: Recombinant CYP17A1 17alpha-hydroxylase-vs-17,20-lyase enzyme assay rating VT-464 lyase-selective (in-vitro biochemical system)
safety.note: Dosed without prednisone for 40 months with cortisol unaffected; later cohorts (Gupta 2018, Madan 2020) also ran steroid-free with no mineralocorticoid excess reported.
safety.quote: The cortisol level was unaffected by the treatment indicating VT-464 selectively did not inhibit CYP17A1 hydroxylase activity
safety.confidence_note: n = 1 for the quoted comparison. Madan 2020 (doi 10.1016/j.clgc.2019.11.002, 17 patients): 'Seviteronel was administered without routine oral steroids', no mineralocorticoid-excess event among the most common AEs; Gupta 2018 (doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-18-0564, 21 patients) abstract lists none either; neither reports cortisol.
safety.judgement: The stated prediction (cortisol spared, no steroid replacement, no mineralocorticoid excess) held, so same. Confusion and tremor (Bardia 2018, Madan 2020) are harms a biochemical assay cannot show, so they are not this track's miss and are already scored contra on the xenograft track. The later, larger steroid-free cohorts change no status, so no further entry.
safety.magnitude_basis: plasma cortisol under 40 months of steroid-free treatment, one patient
safety.population: mCRPC with bone metastases, VT-464 without prednisone
